I used the POSCARs to compare coordination, crystal symmetry, bond-length anisotropy and structural flexibility, alongside chemistry-based predictions trained on the supplied data. I treated the 5 eV cutoff as a separate screening constraint rather than simply maximizing predicted \(d_{ij}\).

My ranked selection is:

| Rank | Candidate | Formula | Structural reasoning |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **c049** | ZnCl₂ | Non-centrosymmetric \(I\bar{4}2d\) framework of corner-linked ZnCl₄ tetrahedra. Framework distortions provide a promising route to a large strain response. |
| 2 | **c048** | ZnCl₂ | Polar \(Pna2_1\) tetrahedral framework, also favorable for mechanically compliant piezoelectric deformation. |
| 3 | **c029** | GeH₃Cl | Polar \(Cmc2_1\) molecular packing combines directional Ge–Cl bonding with relatively compliant intermolecular degrees of freedom. Its saturated Ge coordination favors a wider gap than low-valence germanium compounds. |
| 4 | **c066** | Na₄CO₄ | Monoclinic \(C2\) symmetry, distorted CO₄ tetrahedra and a deformable sodium environment favor a larger response than the more symmetric Na₄CO₄ variants. |
| 5 | **c092** | SF₄ | Non-centrosymmetric \(I\bar{4}2m\) structure with strongly polar S–F bonds and molecular-scale flexibility. Its inferred gap has a larger safety margin, making it preferable to several higher-response but cutoff-sensitive alternatives. |

The inferred gaps are not verified measurements. The ZnCl₂ structures and c066 carry more cutoff uncertainty than c092; their higher predicted piezoelectric responses justify their inclusion.

Final: c049, c048, c029, c066, c092

  f[tag+'_frac']=sum(w[mask])
